docs.preview:
# Contributing

## General Guideline

### Reporting Issues

If you have found what you think is a bug, please [start a discussion](https://github.com/pmndrs/valtio/discussions/new?category=bug-report).

For any usage questions, please [start a discussion](https://github.com/pmndrs/valtio/discussions/new?category=q-a).

### Suggesting New Features

If you are here to suggest a feature, first [start a discussion](https://github.com/pmndrs/valtio/discussions/new?category=ideas) if it does not already exist. From there, we will discuss use-cases for the feature and then finally discuss how it could be implemented.

### Committing

We are applying [conventional commit spec](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) here. In short, that means a commit has to be one of the following types:

Your commit type must be one of the following:

- **feat**: A new feature.
- **fix**: A bug fix.
- **refactor**: A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature.
- **chore**: Changes to the build process, configuration, dependencies, CI/CD pipelines, or other auxiliary tools and libraries.
- **docs**: Documentation-only changes.
- **test**: Adding missing or correcting existing tests.

If you are unfamiliar with the usage of conventional commits,
the short version is to simply specify the type as a first word,
and follow it with a colon and a space, then start your message
from a lowercase letter, like this:

```
feat: add a 'foo' type support
```

You can also specify the scope of the commit in the parentheses after a type:

```
fix(react): change the 'bar' parameter type
```

### Development

If you would like to contribute by fixing an open issue or developing a new feature you can use this suggested workflow:

#### General

1. Fork this repository.
2. Create a new feature branch based off the `main` branch.
3. Follow the [Core](#Core) and/or the [Documentation](#Documentation) guide below and come back to this once done.
4. Run `pnpm run fix:format` to format the code.
5. Git stage your required changes and commit (review the commit guidelines below).
6. Start or continue the relevant discussion, share your fork branch, and wait for maintainer guidance. We don't accept direct PRs, but a maintainer may open a PR from your fork branch for review.

##### Core

1. Run `pnpm install` to install dependencies.
2. Create failing tests for your fix or new feature in the [`tests`](./tests/) folder.
3. Implement your changes.
4. Run `pnpm run build` to build the library. _(Pro-tip: `pnpm run build-watch` runs the build in watch mode)_
5. Run the tests by running `pnpm run test` and ensure that they pass.
6. You can use `pnpm link` to sym-link this package and test it locally on your own project. Alternatively, you may use CodeSandbox CI's canary releases to test the changes in your own project. (requires a PR to be created first)
7. Follow step 4 and onwards from the [General](#General) guide above to bring it to the finish line.

### Pull Requests

We don't accept direct pull requests from contributors. Please use a discussion to report bugs, ask questions, or propose features, and share a branch from your fork when a maintainer asks for code.

If a maintainer opens a pull request from your fork branch, please try to keep it focused in scope and avoid including unrelated commits.

When a pull request is opened from your fork branch, we'll try to get back to you as soon as possible. We may suggest some changes or request improvements, therefore, please check ✅ ["Allow edits from maintainers"](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/creating-a-pull-request-from-a-fork) on your PR.

## Valtio-specific Guideline

##### Documentation

1. Navigate to the [`website`](./website/) folder. (e.g., `cd website`).
2. Run `pnpm install` to install dependencies in the `website` folder.
3. Run `pnpm run dev` to start the dev server.
4. Navigate to [`http://localhost:3000`](http://localhost:3000) to view the documents.
5. Navigate to the [`docs`](./docs/) folder and make necessary changes to the documents.
6. Add your changes to the documents and see them live reloaded in the browser.
7. Follow step 4 and onwards from the [General](#General) guide above to bring it to the finish line.

Thank you for contributing! :heart:

npm install valtio makes proxy-state simple [![Build Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/pmndrs/valtio/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat&colorA=000000&colorB=000000)](https://github.com/pmndrs/valtio/actions/workflows/test.yml?query=branch%3Amain) [![Build Size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/valtio?label=bundle%20size&style=flat&colorA=000000&colorB=000000)](https://bundlephobia.com/result?p=valtio) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/valtio?style=flat&colorA=000000&colorB=000000)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/valtio) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/valtio.svg?style=flat&colorA=000000&colorB=000000)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/valtio) [![Discord Shield](https://img.shields.io/discord/740090768164651008?style=flat&colorA=000000&colorB=000000&label=discord&logo=discord&logoColor=ffffff)](https://discord.gg/poimandres) #### Wrap your state object Valtio turns the object you pass it into a self-aware proxy. ```jsx import { proxy, useSnapshot } from 'valtio' const state = proxy({ count: 0, text: 'hello' }) ``` #### Mutate from anywhere You can make changes to it in the same way you would to a normal js-object. ```jsx setInterval(() => { ++state.count }, 1000) ``` #### React via useSnapshot Create a local snapshot that catches changes. Rule of thumb: read from snapshots in render function, otherwise use the source. The component will only re-render when the parts of the state you access have changed, it is render-optimized. ```jsx // This will re-render on `state.count` change but not on `state.text` change function Counter() { const snap = useSnapshot(state) return (
{snap.count}
) } ```
Note for TypeScript users: Return type of useSnapshot can be too strict. The `snap` variable returned by `useSnapshot` is a (deeply) read-only object. Its type has `readonly` attribute, which may be too strict for some use cases. To mitigate typing difficulties, you might want to loosen the type definition: ```ts declare module 'valtio' { function useSnapshot(p: T): T } ``` See [#327](https://github.com/pmndrs/valtio/issues/327) for more information.
Note: useSnapshot returns a new proxy for render optimization. Internally, `useSnapshot` calls `snapshot` in valtio/vanilla, and wraps the snapshot object with another proxy to detect property access. This feature is based on [proxy-compare](https://github.com/dai-shi/proxy-compare). Two kinds of proxies are used for different purposes: - `proxy()` from `valtio/vanilla` is for mutation tracking or write tracking. - `createProxy()` from `proxy-compare` is for usage tracking or read tracking.
Use of this is for expert users. Valtio tries best to handle `this` behavior but it's hard to understand without familiarity. ```js const state = proxy({ count: 0, inc() { ++this.count }, }) state.inc() // `this` points to `state` and it works fine const snap = useSnapshot(state) snap.inc() // `this` points to `snap` and it doesn't work because snapshot is frozen ``` To avoid this pitfall, the recommended pattern is not to use `this` and prefer arrow function. ```js const state = proxy({ count: 0, inc: () => { ++state.count }, }) ```
If you are new to this, it's highly recommended to use [eslint-plugin-valtio](https://github.com/pmndrs/eslint-plugin-valtio). #### Subscribe from anywhere You can access state outside of your components and subscribe to changes. ```jsx import { subscribe } from 'valtio' // Subscribe to all state changes const unsubscribe = subscribe(state, () => console.log('state has changed to', state), ) // Unsubscribe by calling the result unsubscribe() ``` You can also subscribe to a portion of state. ```jsx const state = proxy({ obj: { foo: 'bar' }, arr: ['hello'] }) subscribe(state.obj, () => console.log('state.obj has changed to', state.obj)) state.obj.foo = 'baz' subscribe(state.arr, () => console.log('state.arr has changed to', state.arr)) state.arr.push('world') ``` To subscribe to a primitive value of state, consider `subscribeKey` in utils. ```jsx import { subscribeKey } from 'valtio/utils' const state = proxy({ count: 0, text: 'hello' }) subscribeKey(state, 'count', (v) => console.log('state.count has changed to', v), ) ``` There is another util `watch` which might be convenient in some cases. ```jsx import { watch } from 'valtio/utils' const state = proxy({ count: 0 }) const stop = watch((get) => { console.log('state has changed to', get(state)) // auto-subscribe on use }) ``` #### Suspend your components Valtio is compatible with React 19 `use` hook. This eliminates all the async back-and-forth, you can access your data directly while the parent is responsible for fallback state and error handling. ```jsx import { use } from 'react' // React 19 // import { use } from 'react18-use' // React 18 const state = proxy({ post: fetch(url).then((res) => res.json()) }) function Post() { const snap = useSnapshot(state) return
{use(snap.post).title}
} function App() { return ( waiting...}> ) } ``` It still suffers from "de-opt", which prevents `useTransition` to work well. To mitigate it, there is a third-party library [use-valtio](https://github.com/valtiojs/use-valtio). #### Holding objects in state without tracking them This may be useful if you have large, nested objects with accessors that you don't want to proxy. `ref` allows you to keep these objects inside the state model. See [#61](https://github.com/pmndrs/valtio/issues/61) and [#178](https://github.com/pmndrs/valtio/issues/178) for more information. When `ref` is passed an existing Valtio proxy, it returns the same proxy and globally marks it as untracked, including in later proxy composition. See the [`ref` API documentation](./docs/api/advanced/ref.mdx) for details. ```js import { proxy, ref } from 'valtio' const state = proxy({ count: 0, dom: ref(document.body), }) ``` #### Update transiently (for often occurring state-changes) You can read state in a component without causing re-render. ```jsx function Foo() { const { count, text } = state // ... ``` Or, you can have more control with subscribing in useEffect. ```jsx function Foo() { const total = useRef(0) useEffect(() => subscribe(state.arr, () => { total.current = state.arr.reduce((p, c) => p + c) }), []) // ... ``` #### Update synchronously By default, state mutations are batched before triggering re-render. Sometimes, we want to disable the batching. The known use case of this is `` [#270](https://github.com/pmndrs/valtio/issues/270). ```jsx function TextBox() { const snap = useSnapshot(state, { sync: true }) return ( (state.text = e.target.value)} /> ) } ``` #### Dev tools You can use [Redux DevTools Extension](https://github.com/reduxjs/redux-devtools) for plain objects and arrays. ```jsx import { devtools } from 'valtio/utils' const state = proxy({ count: 0, text: 'hello' }) const unsub = devtools(state, { name: 'state name', enabled: true }) ```

## How to contribute

### Basic things to know before adding docs

- Docs live in `docs/` folder.
- Website lives in `website/` folder.
- Docs are written in `mdx` format.
- Docs filename shouldn't have spaces.
- Website would generate title and other metadata from graymatter in the file.
- You should be able to render condesandbox inside `mdx` files by simply adding the url for the same
- Once you have a doc, you can add it to the sidebar section by adding it to the nav in `getDocsNav` function inside `website/lib/mdx.ts`

report.overview: Valtio is a TypeScript state-management library for React and vanilla JavaScript applications. Developers mutate ordinary-looking proxy objects, while versioned snapshots and property-access tracking connect those changes to subscribers and React renders. This checkout also contains reactive collection utilities, Redux DevTools integration, a Next.js documentation website, and examples covering counters, todos, undo/redo, and browser-local photo persistence.
report.agent_prompt:
Onboard to Valtio at commit 26d8ca8cb6e5bb3b9516d429e50bc5aab1f42e0d. Treat this brief as a bounded source inspection: tests and CI were inspected, not executed, and test assertions are intended contracts rather than passing results. Reverify relevant source before making changes.

Start with package.json, src/index.ts, src/vanilla.ts, src/react.ts, vitest.config.mts, tsconfig.json, and rollup.config.mjs. The root entrypoint exports vanilla and React APIs; vanilla-only consumers should use valtio/vanilla. Utility barrels separate vanilla helpers from useProxy. The workspace includes the root and website; examples have separate manifests and dependency versions.

Understand the two-proxy design. proxy() tracks writes against the supplied object, recursively wrapping eligible writable values. WeakMaps own proxy identities, internal state, and snapshot caches; a shared version holder supports nested propagation and cycle checks. Setting an equal value normally bails out. Replacing a child removes its old listener relationship before installing the replacement. subscribe() batches callbacks through a Promise microtask unless synchronous notification is requested; its cleanup suppresses queued callbacks. snapshot() caches by version, preserves prototypes, evaluates getters, and recursively snapshots tracked children. Existing snapshot properties are non-writable but configurable, and snapshots remain extensible. ref() preserves identity and globally excludes that identity from tracking in this runtime.

useSnapshot() integrates subscribe() and snapshot() with useSyncExternalStore, then uses proxy-compare to track properties read during rendering. Read snapshots during render and mutate live proxies in actions. Promises are retained as values; React use() handles their consumption. A hook subscribed directly to an old child does not automatically follow replacement at the parent.

Inspect matching tests before edits. Relevant suites cover vanilla replacement, aliases, cycles, descriptors, snapshots, subscriptions, React optimization, async behavior, SSR, utility collections, watch regressions, memory retention, and depth-sensitive snapshot timing. When execution is separately authorized, begin with pnpm run test:spec -- <matching-test-file>, then use test:types, test:lint, and broader checks as warranted. Packaging changes also require built CJS/ESM validation; the configured build matrix currently uses development mode only.

Keep utility changes small. proxyMap and proxySet combine proxied arrays with closure-owned indexes and snapshot caches. watch is deprecated. History comes from valtio-history, and derive documentation describes an external deprecated package. Website MDX compilation reads repository docs, invokes bundling, and emits assets; it requires trusted content. Maintain getDocsNav when adding documentation. Follow existing .ts import extensions, strict types, single quotes, and no semicolons. Do not install, execute, write, publish, or access secrets while operating under the original read-only investigation authorization.

system_map.summary: The primary product is a library with separate vanilla and React runtime boundaries. Its state resides in JavaScript objects and runtime caches; persistence is supplied by consuming applications. Rollup produces publishable CommonJS, ESM, and declaration artifacts, while the documentation website and examples have separate application configurations. The inspected workflows describe validation and package publication, without establishing their execution results.

claims.claim: src/index.ts re-exports vanilla and React APIs; src/utils.ts similarly combines vanilla utilities with React utilities, allowing consumers to choose narrower subpath imports.
The vanilla runtime owns proxyStateMap, refSet, snapCache, proxyCache, and a shared versionHolder; each ProxyState contains the target, ensureVersion, and addListener.

The React layer depends on useSyncExternalStore and proxy-compare's createProxy/isChanged, while the vanilla layer imports only proxy-compare helpers; React and its types are optional peers requiring version 18 or newer.

Package exports select CJS .js/.d.ts artifacts by default and for react-native, or ESM .mjs/.d.mts artifacts for imports; typesVersions provides a fallback declaration for TypeScript versions below 4.5.

Six build scripts select Rollup entrypoints; the config emits ES2018 CJS/ESM bundles and declarations, while postbuild rewrites declaration imports, copies metadata, and makes the dist manifest publishable.
The pnpm workspace includes only the root and website; Vite examples have separate manifests, and their inspected configs enable React plugins, with the starter using the SWC variant.

The website uses Next.js pages with a landing route and statically enumerated /docs/[...slug] pages; its scripts expose next dev/build/start, and styling uses class-based Tailwind dark mode and typography.
Root validation scripts cover formatting, types, lint, and Vitest; release publication builds and publishes from dist, while push/PR preview publication uses pkg-pr-new with example templates.

feature_catalog.summary: The library exposes mutable proxy state, snapshots, subscriptions, and React hooks as its primary developer-facing features. Utilities add reactive collections, cloning, normalization, effects, and debugging. Examples demonstrate complete interactions, while the website provides documentation navigation and theme controls. History and derived-state documentation also introduce external packages, whose implementations are outside this inspection.

claims.claim: proxy() accepts an object or defaults to {}, reuses a cached proxy for the same base object, and wraps eligible assigned children; snapshot() and getVersion() expose current derived state and version information.

subscribe() returns an unsubscribe function and supports batched or synchronous delivery; subscribeKey() adds Object.is filtering for a particular property, and unstable_enableOp() enables set/delete mutation records.

useSnapshot() returns a property-tracked Snapshot<T> with an optional sync flag; useProxy() provides render-time snapshot reads and post-layout live reads, with an explicit React Compiler compatibility caveat.

proxyMap() implements reactive lookup, mutation, iteration, size, and snapshot mutation guards; proxySet() adds reactive Set operations and union/intersection/difference predicates, while proxyMap's getOrInsert methods explicitly throw.

ref() excludes an identity from tracking; deepClone() recursively copies ordinary containers while retaining configured references, and unstable_deepProxy() additionally converts native or proxy Maps/Sets into reactive collections.

watch() runs an effect immediately, tracks proxies passed to get(), and manages cleanup/subscriptions, but is deprecated; devtools() connects to Redux DevTools for state inspection, ACTION updates, time travel, commit, and imported history.

Examples expose counter increment/decrement and independent ticks, array-backed todo add/toggle/delete/filter, and Map-backed todo editing, bulk completion, three filters, and active counts; the history editor exposes undo/redo through valtio-history.

The photo booth captures camera frames, accepts/rejects candidates, selects/deletes saved images, and persists images through localforage; the website exposes MDX docs, a mobile navigation dialog, and localStorage/system-driven dark mode.

data_flow.summary: Object inputs become mutation-tracking proxies backed by identity caches and version propagation. Snapshot creation translates live state into cached read-only properties, and React adds access tracking before rendering. Reactive collections keep indexing state outside their proxied storage arrays. Application and website adapters then translate changes into browser storage, DOM updates, compiled documentation, or extension messages.

claims.claim: proxy(baseObject) validates the object, checks proxyCache, creates and registers its proxy/state tuple, then assigns writable own values through the proxy to initialize nested tracking; this operates on the original base object.

The set trap compares old and incoming identities, removes the previous child relationship, unwraps proxy-compare values, recursively proxies eligible replacements, installs their relationship, writes through Reflect.set, and notifies.

notifyUpdate advances a shared version and sends listeners the new version; child listeners prepend their property to operation paths, while ensureVersion recursively checks child versions when the global check version changes.

snapshot() obtains the target and current version; createSnapshotDefault reuses matching cached snapshots, caches new containers before traversing keys, preserves prototypes/enumerability, evaluates values through Reflect.get, and snapshots tracked children.

useSnapshot() subscribes through useSyncExternalStore, obtains snapshots for client and server reads, reuses the previous snapshot when affected properties are unchanged outside render, and returns a proxy-compare wrapper that records future reads.

proxyMap stores values in proxied data slots and maps keys to slot indexes in a closure; proxySet similarly indexes normalized values. Their epoch properties support structural tracking, and snapshot-index WeakMaps select historical lookup indexes.

The photo booth loads localforage's images into camera.images, then a store subscription writes snapshot images back and redraws controls/images; the localStorage persistence recipe separately serializes application state under the key foo.

Documentation flows from recursively filtered .md/.mdx files through slug generation, filesystem reads, gray-matter parsing, bundleMDX plugins, and emitted assets; getStaticProps supplies compiled code to getMDXComponent for browser rendering.

behavior_traces.summary: These traces follow source execution order across library and application boundaries. Counter startup and mutation demonstrate proxy construction and React notification, while both todo examples show action-to-render paths. The photo booth provides a concrete persistence lifecycle, and the documentation route demonstrates build-time compilation followed by rendering. DevTools and watch illustrate bidirectional external messages and reactive-effect cleanup.

claims.claim: Counter startup: main.tsx imports App → module evaluation calls proxy({number:0}), assigns nested ticks, and starts a 200 ms interval → createRoot renders StrictMode/App → Figure and Ticks call useSnapshot and read separate properties.

Counter increment: ButtonUp's onClick increments state.number → the set trap installs the value and notifyUpdate advances its version → subscribe schedules a microtask → useSnapshot compares affected reads and returns the snapshot used by Figure.

Array todo addition: AddTodoInput.handleSubmit calls actions.addTodo and clears its input → addTodo pushes a generated numeric id into store.todos → useTodos reads useSnapshot(store) and applies the active filter → TodoList maps results into TodoRow.

Map todo addition: form submission prevents default and rejects whitespace-only input → actions.addTodo calls store.todos.set with an id and completed:false → proxyMap.set writes a data slot and increments epoch → useTodos iterates snapshot values and TodoList renders TodoItem.

Photo persistence: window load awaits loadImages then startMediaStream → capture draws video onto canvas and assigns a WebP data URL → acceptance calls saveImage and clears the candidate → the subscription snapshots images into localforage and redraws the gallery; later loadImages restores them.

Documentation navigation: getStaticPaths calls getAllDocs/getSlugs with fallback:false → getStaticProps joins slug segments and calls getDocBySlug/getDocsNav → bundleMDX returns code/frontmatter → Doc renders DocLayout and MDXRenderer, which constructs the compiled component.

DevTools lifecycle: devtools checks its enablement and extension → enables operations and connects → subscription sends snapshots for non-marker changes → ACTION JSON is assigned into live state, while jump messages set a time-travel flag → returned cleanup removes both subscriptions.

watch lifecycle: watch creates cleanup/subscription sets and invokes revalidate → revalidate runs previous cleanups and calls callback(get) → get immediately subscribes newly used proxies → the parent context is restored before awaiting returned work → obsolete subscriptions are removed; cleanup stops further reevaluation.

testing_signals.summary: Tests and CI were inspected, not executed; no passing result or measured coverage is asserted. Vitest runs the tests directory in jsdom with React Testing Library and jest-dom support. Inspected suites cover core graph semantics, React rendering, utility behavior, regressions, and selected performance/memory contracts. This bounded inspection does not establish exhaustive coverage, and the root configuration does not directly include website or example application tests.

claims.claim: Vitest aliases valtio imports to src, uses jsdom, global APIs, tests/setup.ts, and tests as its discovery directory; V8 coverage output is configured, but the inspected CI command is plain test:spec and no coverage threshold appears in this config.

Vanilla tests specify object validation, proxy-cache identity, wrappers, child replacement, descriptors, shadowing __proto__/constructor properties, snapshot reuse/read-only properties, subscription batching, synchronous notification, and queued-callback cancellation.

React optimization tests use render spies, act, fireEvent, and fake timers to specify unchanged-leaf suppression, unwrapping snapshots assigned outside render, non-own deletion behavior, and changing accessed-key dependencies.
SSR tests assert renderToString output for current and nested state; async tests exercise Suspense with promise-backed values but skip those cases when React's use export is unavailable.

Collection suites specify historical snapshot lookup and mutation rejection; deepProxy cases cover object cycles, aliasing, collection normalization, and descriptors. DevTools tests cover unsubscribe and malformed ACTION payloads, and watch regression tests cover synchronous loops and async context isolation.

Memory tests use jest-leak-detector on simple/nested/cyclic proxies and unsubscribed state; the performance test samples 5,000 iterations at depths 4–256 and asserts a log-slope below 0.1 for cached snapshots with subscription, without providing results in this inspection.

Main CI is configured on main pushes and opened/synchronized PRs to install, check formatting/types/lint, run specs, and build; root TypeScript includes src/tests, while root ESLint explicitly ignores examples and website.

Additional workflows configure CJS/ESM artifact testing in development mode, React 18/19/canary/experimental compatibility, and TypeScript 4.5–5.9 type checks with compatibility patches; the production build-matrix option is commented out.

risk_map.summary: These are source observations and explicitly labeled hypotheses, not confirmed vulnerabilities. The inspected core primarily manages in-process state; external trust boundaries appear in DevTools messages, browser camera/storage adapters, and documentation compilation. Identity, snapshot descriptors, global internal customization, and dependency-version drift are major correctness boundaries. Missing execution evidence leaves configured tests and deployment compatibility unresolved.

claims.claim: DevTools is a state-write and state-export boundary: it sends snapshots to an extension and Object.assigns parsed ACTION/jump/import data into live proxies. ACTION parsing is caught, but jump-state parsing is outside that catch; enabled:true can override production-default disablement.

The docs pipeline assumes trusted repository content: bundleMDX compiles source/imports, oEmbed processing accepts returned HTML, and getMDXComponent constructs executable components. Slugs are statically enumerated with fallback:false, so the inspected route is not an arbitrary public file-read endpoint.

Photo-booth persistence writes are not awaited or caught in the store subscription, restored images are assigned without schema validation, and camera failure is only logged. Its startMediaStream implementation assigns srcObject without a stream-stop cleanup.

Hypothesis: cyclic input can overflow deepClone's un-memoized recursion; self-referential Map/Set input can similarly recurse in unstable_deepProxy because collection branches run before memo lookup/registration. Inspected deepClone tests cover ordinary containers, and deepProxy cycle cases cover ordinary objects rather than cyclic collections.

Internal customization has runtime-wide blast radius: unstable_replaceInternalFunction replaces shared factories/comparators, unstable_enableOp changes shared operation generation, and ref(existingProxy) marks that proxy identity globally rather than just one parent property.

Snapshot immutability has deliberate limits: properties are non-writable but configurable and containers remain extensible; ref values remain shared references. Separately, useSnapshot on a captured child continues observing that identity after its parent replaces the child.

Documentation and application versions drift: subscribe-ops documents resolve/reject operations although the source Op type only contains set/delete; architecture notes describe promise unwrapping despite the v2 migration guide removing it. The website requests valtio ^1.5.2, and the Map todo uses legacy react-dom render with React 18 dependencies.

Production-specific behavior has a configured validation gap: the artifact matrix includes development only and marks production cases skipped; the inspected main workflow runs root tests/build, whose type and lint boundaries exclude website/example source.

extension_points.summary: Extensions primarily compose exported functions rather than register plugins. Utility barrels and separate package entrypoints define the public surface, while unstable internal APIs permit deeper runtime customization. Application actions, computed getters, persistence subscriptions, and external history packages provide higher-level composition. Website navigation and MDX plugin arrays offer separate documentation extension points.

claims.claim: New vanilla helpers plug into src/vanilla/utils.ts, React helpers into src/react/utils.ts, and their combined exports reach valtio/utils through src/utils.ts.

unstable_replaceInternalFunction supports wrappers around objectIs, newProxy, canProxy, createSnapshot, and createHandler; unstable_getInternalStates exposes the runtime maps, sets, and version holder.
unstable_enableOp accepts true, false, or a custom operation factory; subscribe exposes generated operation tuples, and nested listeners prefix paths for integrations consuming mutation records.

deepClone and unstable_deepProxy accept a getRefSet provider, allowing caller-controlled identities to bypass reconstruction; unstable_deepProxy rebuilds descriptors and prototypes before wrapping ordinary containers.

Application actions and computed getters are natural composition points: todo actions directly mutate proxies, while class/getter examples derive values without a reducer registry; persistence can attach through subscribe.

Undo/redo extends state through external valtio-history's proxyWithHistory wrapper; derive documentation points to external derive-valtio and recommends migration to valtio-reactive rather than adding a built-in derive implementation.

Documentation files provide frontmatter titles/metadata, prepareDoc builds links, getDocsMap indexes navigation by each final slug segment, and getDocsNav explicitly chooses sidebar entries; equal final segments therefore share the same map key.

Website content transforms plug into bundleMDX's remark/rehype arrays and esbuild loaders; remarkCodeSandboxURLUpdater accepts configurable query parameters. Library packaging separately extends through Rollup's entry aliases and config-* selection.

agent_handoff.summary: Start with the core runtime and the test that specifies the requested behavior, then inspect packaging or application adapters only when relevant. Preserve identity, version, listener, and snapshot contracts when editing the central proxy implementation. Tests and CI were inspected, not executed; commands below are future validation choices only when execution is authorized. The inventory and this investigation are bounded, and public documentation contains some version drift that must be checked against implementation.

claims.claim: Read src/index.ts, src/vanilla.ts, and src/react.ts first for core changes: they establish exports, proxy/snapshot ownership, subscription timing, and React's access-tracked external-store adapter.

For authorized future validation, start with pnpm run test:spec -- <relevant-test-file>, then test:types/test:lint; root test aggregates test:* scripts, and tests import valtio through aliases resolving to source rather than built artifacts.

Tests and CI were inspected, not executed in this brief. Their configured discovery and commands describe intended validation; jsdom tests and renderToString assertions do not establish website/example end-to-end browser behavior.

Preserve replacement and alias semantics: tests require replacement identity, unchanged previous objects, own-key order, retained shared members, and queued child operation delivery before parent replacement.

Match strict TypeScript conventions, noUncheckedIndexedAccess/exactOptionalPropertyTypes, isolated declarations, explicit .ts source imports, single quotes, and no semicolons; declaration packaging rewrites source import extensions for published consumers.

Use proxyMap/proxySet for reactive native-collection-like behavior, read snapshots and mutate live state, and account for globally marked refs and replaced child references; native Map/Set and Promise values are not recursively proxied by the default eligibility rule.

For docs/example work, inspect that surface's manifest and runtime API usage instead of assuming the root version; maintain getDocsNav for new pages, verify v2 promise semantics against source, and recognize history as an external package.

Packaging changes affect six entry builds and declaration patching; inspect the CJS/ESM workflow before selecting validation. CONTRIBUTING requests focused tests and discussion-led contributions, with maintainer-created PRs rather than direct contributor PRs.
